clue.text: Translation of paper, a rash translation

indicators.note: the second translation tells us to render these letters into another form, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A hasty, careless rendering of some document into another language.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'translation' signals the anagram of PAPER, A and RASH; the first is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A restatement of a text in other words is a kind of rendering, much like a free translation.

explanation.surface: A fish with a sulky face.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small fish of the cod family; to push out the lips sulkily is to look cross.

clue.text: Right suggestion to Salome after her dance?

definitions.text: suggestion to Salome after her dance?

explanation.surface: Advice to Salome once she has finished her famous dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Salome's dance of the seven veils left her undressed, so she should get her clothes back on.
explanation.definitionFit: To right a wrong is to remedy it; split as re-dress it urges putting clothes on again.

clue.text: "To be or not to be" is a verb, for instance

definitions.text: "To be or not to be" is a verb, for instance

parts.words: "To be or not to be" is a verb, for instance
parts.note: Hamlet's line is a fragment of his soliloquy, while a verb is a grammatical class of word such as a noun or adjective

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson using Hamlet's famous words.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb is one of the grammatical word classes; Hamlet's line is a section of an oration.

clue.text: Engineer gets taken to court and sent out again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
gets taken to court means is sued

explanation.surface: A technician is prosecuted and then dispatched once more.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute or publish something a second time is to put it out anew.

explanation.surface: Lord Raglan may be the record holder.
explanation.walkthrough: A raglan is a type of sleeve running to the collar; a record's cardboard cover holds the disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A raglan is a style of arm covering on a garment; a cardboard jacket holds a vinyl disc.

clue.text: Point to humble dwelling that's close

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
a hut is a simple, modest home

explanation.surface: Directions to a modest cottage nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: To close a door is to make it fast, the same as when it is described as not open.

parts.note: read as one who ravages, to harry being to lay waste, and also as a cross-country runner

explanation.surface: An overwhelmingly good sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devastating' suggests brilliant, but to harry is to ravage.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-country runner bears this name, and so does one who lays waste to land.

clue.text: Sailors get the last word in every French competition

indicators.note: in places sailors and the last word inside the French for every

parts.note: tout is French for every or all
RN is the Royal Navy
amen is the closing word of a prayer

explanation.surface: Navy men have the final say in every French contest.
explanation.walkthrough: RN (Royal Navy) plus AMEN go inside TOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a series of contests between competitors.

indicators.note: mind-bending suggests twisting the letters of endure and mind into a new shape

explanation.surface: Putting up with something that warps the mind, as a soldier once did.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers who dig tunnels under enemy positions.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappers dug tunnels beneath enemy walls, which is literally what weakening from below means.

clue.text: This foreign lady's no end of an imposter

indicators.note: no end of tells us to drop the final letter of the word for imposter

parts.note: a fraud is a cheat or imposter

explanation.surface: A woman from abroad who is a complete charlatan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' cuts the last letter D from FRAUD.
explanation.definitionFit: German speakers address a married woman this way, as English uses Mrs.

parts.note: read as a man who ruled in his father's place and was later crowned George IV, not yet a full monarch

explanation.surface: Someone telling George to wait as they have not finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The future George IV ruled for his ill father from 1811 to 1820 before succeeding him.
explanation.definitionFit: The son who governed for George III became George IV, so he was a king not yet complete.

parts.note: a vet is a veterinary surgeon
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A doctor finally makes it to the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to forbid it, which is what a ruling of rejection does.

parts.note: read as a coin worth four crowns in old British money, a pound coin of gold; also the Crown means a monarch

explanation.surface: A royal headpiece that used to count as four of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A crown was five shillings, so four crowns made a pound, the value of this old gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: This gold coin was worth one pound, which equals four five-shilling crowns; the word also names a monarch.

clue.text: Young man and old can't see differently

indicators.note: differently means arranging the letters of old, can't and see another way

explanation.surface: Youth and age see things in different ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' signals the anagram of OLD, CANT and SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a youth between childhood and adulthood.

parts.note: taken as written
an aster is a daisy-like flower, as in Michaelmas daisy

explanation.surface: Someone lamenting that Daisy has died.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a catastrophe, a terrible event.

parts.note: a worker ant is the crossword's usual worker
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A council employee has the advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTRIM is a county of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.

parts.note: read both as money earned on savings and as a stake or concern in something

explanation.surface: A business run to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concern' looks like a business, but it means a share or involvement.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that savings earn is a profit; a stake in something is a concern.

clue.text: Slavishly I tend to want you back

parts.note: to want is to lack

indicators.note: back says the old word for you is read backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: Someone admits a servile devotion and longs to have a person return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns YE into EY.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to act as a servile footman is to wait on someone slavishly.

explanation.surface: Giving a gift of a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' here is something that flows, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Present means existing now; a stream of water is something that flows.

clue.text: Prop up and muddle up dinner

indicators.note: to muddle the words is to jumble their letters into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone supports a table and messes up the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddle' signals the anagram of UP and DINNER; the first 'up' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To support from beneath is to strengthen a foundation, as when shoring up a wall.

clue.text: Girl in dock put up an umbrella

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the letters are read from bottom to top
in places the girl's name inside the word for dock

parts.note: to lop is to dock or cut off
Sara is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl in the dock raises an umbrella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts SARA inside LOP, giving LOSARAP, and 'put up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella giving shade from the sun.

clue.text: Kind of piece shown in colour

indicators.note: shown in places the piece inside the word for colour

parts.note: a hue is a colour
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A sort of artwork displayed in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' looks like 'sort of'; 'Kind' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind means compassionate, showing mercy.

parts.note: strict means tightly controlled
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Complaints about a river whose flow is tightly controlled.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A stricture is a severe critical remark, a censure.

indicators.note: say signals that the word for a pot is to be spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: an urn is a pot or vase

explanation.surface: Gambling to take the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pronunciation the word for the vase rhymes exactly with the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To win money is to gain it, as wages are gained.

explanation.surface: A name like Mark or Leo, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo is one of the twelve zodiac constellations.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark is a symbol; Leo is one of the twelve divisions of the zodiac.

explanation.surface: Is the beer still flat?
explanation.definitionFit: Still is an intensifier as in 'better still'; flat means level, smooth with no bumps.

parts.note: read as a pianist who was also a prime minister: the Polish virtuoso who led his country in 1919

explanation.surface: A leading concert pianist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'premier' looks like 'top-ranked', but means prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: This celebrated Polish pianist became his country's prime minister after the First World War.

explanation.surface: Something built for a more superior bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is one who bets, not 'superior'; the totalisator is a betting system.
explanation.definitionFit: The totalisator is a pool-betting system made for punters; to bear also means to carry a load.

clue.text: Resolve, then, to plan sporting contest

indicators.note: to resolve is to re-solve, breaking the words then, to and plan apart and reassembling them

explanation.surface: A determination to organise a games event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolve' signals the anagram of THEN, TO and PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This athletics event combines five disciplines into one competition.
